request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Pallas by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Core Rust Libraries, Year 2, including maintenance, community support, and AI-friendly documentation/integration resources over 12 months.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve and a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee, totaling 540,750 ADA.

Pallas is a collection of Rust crates implementing Cardano primitives including CBOR encoding, cryptographic operations, mini-protocol networking, multi-era ledger traversal, transaction building, and address handling.
Pallas is used as shared infrastructure by projects including Aiken, Dolos, Lucid, Oura, Mithril, Amaru, UTxO-RPC, and others.
Pallas has over 649 pull requests, 199 stars, 91 forks, 60 contributors, and 214,446 crates.io downloads.
The maintainer scope covers codebase maintenance, community support, and AI-driven development workflow compatibility improvements.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposer states the requested withdrawal does not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

Audit, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, with administration fees covering oversight.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

Intersect will use a Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role thresholds, and an external Oversight Committee consisting of six named entities.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month continuation of Pallas open-source maintenance by TxPipe, submitted by Intersect, with stated governance process support, NCL compliance, smart-contract-based fund administration, and oversight arrangements.
